sentences.text: Altispinax was a large predatory theropod dinosaur belonging to the class Reptilia that lived between 140 and 133 million years ago in what is now East Sussex, England.
The holotype fossil of Altispinax is catalogued as NHMUK PV R 1828 and consists of three posterior dorsal vertebrae with very high spines, inspiring the Latin name meaning 'high with spines'.
Friedrich von Huene established the genus Altispinax in 1923, naming the type species Altispinax dunkeri based on these vertebrae.
Gregory Paul tentatively estimated in 1988 that Altispinax weighed one tonne and was shorter than the eight-meter-long type specimen of Acrocanthosaurus atokensis.
Ralph Molnar suggested that the two vertebrae closest to the skull in Altispinax are fused and interpreted this fusion as evidence of an injury to a back frill that healed from behind.
Fossil collector Samuel Husbands Beckles discovered nodules containing dinosaur bones near Battle, East Sussex, probably in the early 1850s, and Richard Owen reported the fossils in 1856.

The species name dunkeri honors paleontologist Wilhelm Dunker, who discovered a tooth in Deister years prior, and the type specimen of that tooth was added to the University of Marburg collection under catalog number UM 84.
Darren Naish proposed in 2003 that the gap between the front spines was natural rather than the result of injury.
The classification of Altispinax is debated, with placements ranging from Eustreptospondylidae to Allosauroidea, though most researchers currently place it in Tetanurae incertae sedis.

Altispinax was once considered a nomen dubium because no relationship could be proven between the type vertebrae and a single tooth previously assigned to the genus, as later research suggested the tooth was not diagnostic.
George Olshevsky named the genus Becklespinax in 1991 for the Altispinax vertebrae to honor the original discoverer, and the name Metriacanthosaurus is considered a modern synonym of Becklespinax.
Four additional species were named within the genus Altispinax before being reclassified into other genera, including Valdoraptor for Altispinax oweni and Metriacanthosaurus for Altispinax parkeri.
Altispinax lived during the early Cretaceous period, approximately 133 million years ago in the Valanginian stage in what is now Europe.
